text: The idea was not entirely new. In September 1939, a memo circulated by the Director of Naval Intelligence, Admiral John Godfrey, listed dozens of ways to deceive the enemy. Historians have noted that it bore the hallmarks of his personal assistant, a young officer named Ian Fleming, the future creator of James Bond.
